gaps.note: In the paper m = h^3 = 1000000 (line 656) and the bound used is m<2^{20} (line 1332); 1000000 > 2^19 = 524288, so mu<2^19 is false. The correct statement is mu<2^{20}, which still gives ln mu<20 (ln 2<1).

gaps.quote: a forward invocation from $X$ to $Y$ subtracts $x_S$ from $y_S$
gaps.note: The paper's Lemma scalar-motifs (line 729-731) says a forward invocation changes y_S to y_S + x_S, i.e. it adds x_S to y_S. The page itself then identifies it with the shear H <- H+D, which adds, so 'subtracts' is inconsistent with the page and wrong. Also the paper's forward, inverse, forward schedule sends (X,Y) to (-Y,X), an exchange only in the bit construction.

gaps.quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$, so it is exact for any initial auxiliary contents.
gaps.note: The page never says how the scalar bank invocation (one scalar per triple S) becomes a shear of address fields H and D on arrays; in the paper this passes through frame identities and role streams applied to every row, including scratch roles. The identification is asserted, not derived.

gaps.term: why smaller calls have width mu^(d-1)
gaps.quote: At depth $d$, the $s$ smaller calls are interchanges of width $\mu^{d-1}$ on streams of volume $V/W$
gaps.note: The page never says that H and D are each cut into mu consecutive sub-fields of width mu^(d-1) and that each vertex matrix acts on these mu sub-fields (paper line 1395-1406, 1531), so the reader cannot see why edge rank a gives a interchanges of exactly this width.

gaps.quote: Each smaller call acts on one of the $W$ [wire streams](role-streams.md), each of volume $V/W$.
gaps.note: The paper's Proposition power-interchange (line 1475-1486) needs a row field preceding both chunks whose length is divisible by W^k; this is what makes the W streams of equal shape at every depth. The page omits this hypothesis, and the arbitrary-width O(Vu^tau) claim needs padding of rows (Lemma chunk-swap, line 1631-1643), neither of which is mentioned.
